$comment: Inventory manifest for the NVIDIA docs RAG mini-project. Generated 2026-08-18. Metadata from filesystem; stack and config verified by parsing NVIDIA_LLM.ipynb after OneDrive hydration.

project.name: nvidia-docs-rag
project.title: Conversational RAG over NVIDIA documentation
project.one_liner: Crawls the docs.nvidia.com sitemap, indexes it four ways (2 embedding backends x 2 chunk sizes), and serves a conversational retrieval chain over the result.
project.purpose_note: Retained deliberately as an interview-discussion project: it is a controlled comparison across embedding backends and chunk sizes, not a single happy-path pipeline.

corpus.discovery: sitemap index (NVIDIA.xml) -> langchain SitemapLoader with filter_urls
corpus.pages_evidence: tqdm progress line in error_log.txt: 'Fetching pages: 22%|##1 | 12736/59016 [03:00<11:34, 66.65it/s]'
corpus.known_failures: PDF endpoints under /deeplearning/nccl/archives/ failed and were skipped; see error_log.txt

runtime_environment.note: Executed inside an NVIDIA NGC TensorFlow container

judge_model.mechanism: ragas.llms.LangchainLLM wrapper; each metric's .llm reassigned to a locally-served model
judge_model.rationale: RAGAS defaults to OpenAI for every metric evaluation. Self-hosting removes both the per-run API cost and the data-egress exposure, making repeated evaluation across configurations affordable.

evaluation.also_present: AzureOpenAIEmbeddings imported in cell 142 — a third embedding backend beyond ada-002 and all-mpnet-base-v2.
evaluation.design_note: context_precision and context_recall isolate retrieval quality; faithfulness and answer_relevancy isolate generation quality. That separation is what makes the vector-store and chunk-size comparison attributable rather than end-to-end only.

qualitative_comparison.location: cells 106-140, section 'Competitive comparisons of LLM and Retrievers'
qualitative_comparison.what_it_produced: Saved generated answers across the retriever x generator grid (Chroma retrievers, FAISS retrievers) x (gpt-3.5-turbo, Llama-2-7b-chat-hf), available for side-by-side reading.
qualitative_comparison.coverage: 51 of 120 code cells carry saved output

results_status.why_not: The RAGAS section failed at import: "ImportError: cannot import name 'AzureOpenAIEmbeddings' from 'langchain.embeddings'" (cells 142, 143). Library drift, not a design gap.
results_status.author_was_aware: Cell 141 markdown reads: 'Note this requires OpenAIEmbeddings in the langchain package. Currently there are issues using ...'
results_status.related_breakage: 5 cells fail with "AttributeError: module 'openai' has no attribute 'error'" — the openai SDK v1.0 removal of the openai.error namespace. 7 code cells error in total; both causes are upstream releases from late 2023.
results_status.fix: AzureOpenAIEmbeddings moved to the langchain_openai package; openai.error became typed exceptions on the client in SDK v1.x. Pin contemporaneous versions or update the two import sites.
results_status.recommended_next_step: Unblock the imports and re-run to persist a table of the 5 metrics x 7 built index configurations. Stores already exist and the judge is self-hosted, so the run is compute-only with no paid API spend. Highest-value remaining work on the project.
results_status.correction_history: An earlier pass of this manifest stated the evaluation was 'built but never run' and that no benchmark existed. Both were wrong: the qualitative comparison ran and saved outputs, and the RAGAS cells executed but errored. Corrected 2026-08-18 after inspecting per-cell execution counts and error outputs.

author_note.$comment: Author's recollection of the build period, recorded as context for the failed cells. Not a forensic finding — the notebook itself attributes nothing to these events.
author_note.note: I built the OpenAI indexes during the week of 20 November 2023 — which turned out to be the week OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman, Microsoft moved to hire him, and he was back as CEO a few days later. Everyone pivoted to Azure-hosted OpenAI overnight, and AzureOpenAIEmbeddings was being shuffled between LangChain packages while I was trying to import it. The openai SDK v1.0 rewrite had landed a couple of weeks before that and removed the openai.error namespace, which accounts for the rest of the failed cells. A weird week to be building on that stack.

quantization.summary: Llama-2-7B did not fit unquantized on available hardware. Two independent quantized-inference paths are implemented, because the CUDA quantization stack does not run on Apple Silicon.

paths.config: GGUF-quantized model with n_gpu_layers offload, n_ctx, n_batch; Metal/MPS backend
paths.location: NVIDIA_LLM.ipynb — LlamaCpp x3, gguf, n_gpu_layers, mps
paths.rationale: bitsandbytes is CUDA-only and cannot run on M1, so fitting the 7B model locally required a different toolchain entirely.

fine_tuning.result: Zero matches across all 177 cells of NVIDIA_LLM.ipynb and zero in test.ipynb.
fine_tuning.conclusion: No LoRA/PEFT adapter training is present. The work is quantized INFERENCE, not QLoRA fine-tuning. Strict QLoRA means a 4-bit NF4 base with trained LoRA adapters; what exists here is 8-bit bitsandbytes and GGUF quantization to fit the model in memory.
fine_tuning.recommended_phrasing: Describe as: 8-bit quantization on CUDA plus llama.cpp/GGUF on Apple Silicon, to run Llama-2-7B under a hard memory constraint. Accurate, and a stronger claim than QLoRA because it shows the same constraint solved twice on different toolchains.
fine_tuning.caveat: The 'hf4' directory naming refers to the HuggingFace embedding variant, not 4-bit quantization. Contents of mini-projects/nlp_complete.zip remain unchecked and could contain additional work.
fine_tuning.correction_history: An earlier pass of this manifest reported no quantization at all. That was a search error: it grepped the module name 'bitsandbytes' and 4-bit parameters ('load_in_4bit', 'bnb_4bit_*'), while the code uses the class 'BitsAndBytesConfig' with 8-bit parameters. Corrected 2026-08-18.

experiment_matrix.$comment: Vector stores built across two embedding backends and two chunk sizes, in two store engines. One cell was never built.

missing.note: Absent. Chroma's openai_100 store is the largest artifact at 17.9 GiB, so this cell was plausibly skipped on embedding cost or disk grounds.

observations.note: faiss_hf_index_600/index.pkl and faiss_openAI_index_600/index.pkl are identical in size (74198719). Consistent with one shared docstore over the same 600-char chunking, differing only in the vectors in index.faiss — i.e. a controlled comparison holding chunking fixed while varying the embedding model.
Moving chunk_size 100 -> 600 shrinks each store roughly 6-7x, consistently across both engines and both backends. With chunk_overlap fixed at 20, larger chunks mean far fewer vectors.
At equal chunk size, the OpenAI stores are ~2.4x larger than the HuggingFace ones (ada-002 is 1536-dim vs all-mpnet-base-v2 at 768-dim — 2x — plus Chroma parquet overhead).
Crawl first (2023-10-27), Chroma stores next (Nov 20-26), FAISS stores in one tight session (Nov 22). Notebook last touched Nov 28.

steps: Load NVIDIA.xml sitemap index via langchain SitemapLoader (filter_urls as in notebook), continue_on_failure=True.
Split with RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter at chunk_size 100 or 600, chunk_overlap 20.
Persist to Chroma or FAISS under the corresponding directory name.
reproduction.cost_warning: Re-embedding ~59k pages at chunk_size=100 with ada-002 is a substantial paid API run. The OpenAI stores are the expensive cells to rebuild; the HuggingFace ones are compute-only.
reproduction.drift_warning: docs.nvidia.com has changed since 2023-10-27. A re-crawl will NOT reproduce these stores byte-for-byte, which is the main argument for preserving the artifacts rather than relying on regeneration.

preservation_plan.git: Source layer only — notebooks, NVIDIA.xml, error_log.txt, manifest.json, README. ~13 MB.
preservation_plan.dvc: All seven vector stores (~32.7 GiB) tracked by DVC, remote on Google Drive.
preservation_plan.dvc_cache_note: Set cache.type = reflink,hardlink,symlink,copy before `dvc add`. The volume is APFS, so reflinks make `dvc add` near-zero-cost on space; the default copy behavior would double 32.7 GiB against limited free disk.
